validation_sources.roles/host/tasks/validate-interpreted-in:
---
# These values become directives, not argv. Quote-free multiline input would
# let an inventory value add an unrelated root write to the consumer's config.
- name: Validate billet_guest_dns_servers as a list
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: billet_guest_dns_servers is sequence and billet_guest_dns_servers is not string and billet_guest_dns_servers is not mapping
    fail_msg: billet_guest_dns_servers must be a list of IPv4 or IPv6 literals.

- name: Validate each billet_guest_dns_servers literal
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: item | junioryono.billet.ip_literal
    fail_msg: billet_guest_dns_servers must contain only IPv4 or IPv6 literals.
  loop: "{{ billet_guest_dns_servers }}"

- name: Validate each SMTP member as a single line without controls
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: lookup('ansible.builtin.vars', item) | string | junioryono.billet.single_line
    fail_msg: "{{ item }} must be a single line without control characters."
  loop: [billet_smtp_host, billet_smtp_port, billet_smtp_username, billet_smtp_password, billet_alert_from, billet_alert_email]
  # Never print a credential, even when its grammar is refused. The loop label
  # and diagnostic carry only its inventory name.
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item }}"

- name: Validate billet_smtp_host
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: billet_smtp_host | junioryono.billet.smtp_host
    fail_msg: billet_smtp_host must be a DNS hostname or IP literal.

- name: Validate billet_smtp_port
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: billet_smtp_port | junioryono.billet.port
    fail_msg: billet_smtp_port must be a decimal port from 1 to 65535.

- name: Validate billet_alert_from
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: billet_alert_from == '' or billet_alert_from | junioryono.billet.mailbox
    fail_msg: billet_alert_from must be empty or one unquoted mailbox address.

- name: Validate billet_alert_email
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: billet_alert_email == '' or billet_alert_email | junioryono.billet.mailbox
    fail_msg: billet_alert_email must be empty or one unquoted mailbox address.

- name: Validate guest network configuration literals
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - item.name is match('^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,14}\Z')
      - item.name not in ['.', '..']
      - item.address | junioryono.billet.ip_literal(4)
      - item.dhcp_start | junioryono.billet.ip_literal(4)
      - item.dhcp_end | junioryono.billet.ip_literal(4)
      - item.netmask | junioryono.billet.ip_literal(4)
      - item.prefix | string is match('^([0-9]|[12][0-9]|3[0-2])\Z')
    fail_msg: billet_networks must contain literal interface names, IPv4 addresses and decimal prefixes.
  loop: "{{ billet_networks }}"

- name: Validate billet_guest_denied_ipv4
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: item | junioryono.billet.ip_network_literal(4)
    fail_msg: billet_guest_denied_ipv4 must contain IPv4 network literals.
  loop: "{{ billet_guest_denied_ipv4 }}"

- name: Validate billet_guest_denied_ipv6
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: item | junioryono.billet.ip_network_literal(6)
    fail_msg: billet_guest_denied_ipv6 must contain IPv6 network literals.
  loop: "{{ billet_guest_denied_ipv6 }}"

- name: Validate guest firewall port literals
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: item | junioryono.billet.firewall_port
    fail_msg: billet_guest_host_tcp_ports, billet_guest_host_udp_ports and billet_image_verify_port must contain ports from 1 to 65535, port ranges or service names.
  loop: "{{ billet_guest_host_tcp_ports + billet_guest_host_udp_ports + [billet_image_verify_port] }}"

- name: Validate billet_firecracker_version for versioned destinations
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: billet_firecracker_version is match('^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\Z')
    fail_msg: billet_firecracker_version must be a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release.

{"ansible.builtin.set_fact":{"billet_smtp_owned":"{{
  billet_smtp_managed.stat.exists or
  (
    billet_smtp_config.stat.exists and
    (
      (
        billet_smtp_existing_lines | length > 0 and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[0] == '# Managed by junioryono.billet.host. Disable billet_alert_email to remove this file.'
      ) or
      (
        billet_smtp_existing_lines | length == 13 and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[0:8] == [
          'defaults',
          'auth on',
          'tls on',
          'tls_starttls on',
          'tls_trust_file /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt',
          'logfile /var/log/msmtp.log',
          '',
          'account default'
        ] and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[8] is match('^host .+$') and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[9] is match('^port .+$') and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[10] is match('^from .+$') and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[11] is match('^user .+$') and
        billet_smtp_existing_lines[12] is match('^password .+$')
      )
    )
  )
}}"},"name":"Classify billet-owned SMTP configuration"}

definitions.tasks/allocate-recovery.yml / Allocate a:
{"ansible.builtin.command":{"argv":["/bin/sh","-c","set -u
root=$1
stamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S) || { echo "the stamp could not be drawn: date exited $?" >&2; exit 1; }
case "$stamp" in
  [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]T[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;;
  *) echo "the stamp '$stamp' is not <YYYYMMDD>T<HHMMSS>" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 5 ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  suffix=$(sh -c "$2") || { echo "the suffix generator exited non-zero on attempt $attempt" >&2; exit 1; }
  case "$suffix" in
    [0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
    *) echo "the suffix generator printed '$suffix', not eight lowercase hex digits" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  d="$root/recovery-$stamp-$suffix"
  if reason=$(mkdir -m 0700 "$d" 2>&1); then
    printf '%s\n' "$d"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ -e "$d" ] || [ -L "$d" ]; then
    continue
  fi
  echo "attempt $attempt: mkdir $d failed and the name is absent: $reason" >&2
  exit 1
done
echo "five names collided under $root; the allocator is exhausted" >&2
exit 1

billet-images-refresh.service.j2.writes: No shell redirection. billet images refresh owns kernel/image staging and durable installation, outside preventive operand admission per R7.2; the template supplies only constant argv and writable roots.
billet-images-refresh.service.j2.text:
# One check that this node's guest images are current, and a pull if not.
#
# ENABLED BY THE PACKAGE, with billet-upgrade.timer, and that is the one exception
# to the package enabling nothing. The rule exists so that installing billet
# cannot connect a machine to GitHub before its config says something true, and
# this connects nothing: it reads the signed image channel, and it exits doing
# nothing on a host that boots no firecracker guests and under
# `release: {automatic: false}`. What it is for is the deployment nobody visits: a
# node whose images age past GitHub's runner window launches nothing, and a timer
# that was never enabled looks exactly like one that is working right up until
# that day. `billet check` reports a firecracker node whose timer is not enabled.
#
#   systemctl disable --now billet-images-refresh.timer     # to opt a host out
#
# `billet local up` ENABLES AND ARMS THE TIMER TOO, on a firecracker node, as its
# last step, exactly as it does the backup timer on a control-plane host, and
# reports rather than fails when it cannot, because a host converged from a
# tarball ran no postinstall; the timer is deliberately not part of the unit
# plan `up`/`down` prove and unwind.
[Unit]
Description=billet guest image refresh
Documentation=https://github.com/junioryono/billet/blob/main/docs/operating/guest-images.md
After=network-online.target docker.service
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot

# ROOT, AS THE NODE IS: a pull maps RBD images, installs the paired kernel under
# /var/lib/billet/kernels, and boot-verifies the generation under the jailer,
# which needs /dev/kvm, TAP devices and cgroups.
User=root
Group=root

ExecStart=/usr/bin/billet images refresh --config /etc/billet/billet.yaml

# A PULL IS A FIFTEEN-GIGABYTE DOWNLOAD, AN IMPORT AND A BOOT, so the bound is
# generous; the command itself does nothing when nothing is due.
TimeoutStartSec=7200

# BEHIND THE JOBS, not beside them: this is maintenance on a machine whose point
# is running somebody's build.
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=idle

# The kernel lock, the staging directory and the jailer are the writable paths a
# pull needs; the config is read-only.
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/billet /var/tmp/billet-images -/srv/jailer
ReadOnlyPaths=/etc/billet
# The pull maps RBD devices and the probe boots under the jailer, which creates
# cgroups through sysfs; ProtectKernelTunables would remount those read-only.
ProtectKernelModules=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
LockPersonality=true
SystemCallArchitectures=native

billet-images-refresh.timer.j2.writes: No fixed-path output or shell redirection; consumer applies constant service/timer policy or typed network data. The template destination is separately admitted.
billet-images-refresh.timer.j2.text:
# When billet-images-refresh.service runs. Enabled by the package; the service
# says why.
#
#   systemctl disable --now billet-images-refresh.timer     # to opt a host out
#
# DAILY, WITH THE DECISION IN THE COMMAND RATHER THAN THE CALENDAR. The guest
# image is built centrally once a week, and GitHub stops handing jobs to a runner
# about thirty days after a newer release ships, so what matters is not when this
# fires but that a new generation is on the cluster within a day of being
# published. `billet images refresh` compares the channel's build time with the
# newest generation imported and does nothing while nothing newer is published,
# so a daily tick costs one signed statement and one question of the cluster,
# and pulls only when there is something to pull.
[Unit]
Description=billet guest image refresh, daily
Documentation=https://github.com/junioryono/billet/blob/main/docs/operating/guest-images.md

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily

# SPREAD, because a site's nodes all pulling the same fifteen-gigabyte image at
# 00:00:00 is one release asset fetched N times at once and N boot-verifications
# competing for the same cluster.
RandomizedDelaySec=2h

# A MISSED RUN IS RUN: a node that was off for the day would otherwise wait
# another, and the runner window does not.
Persistent=true

Unit=billet-images-refresh.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

billet-node.service.j2.writes: No shell redirection. RuntimeDirectory is systemd-owned; the node command owns registration, TLS renewal and custody writes through existing Go durable file paths, rechecked at closing. Runtime footprints are R7.2 scope.
billet-node.service.j2.text:
[Unit]
Description=billet compute host
Documentation=https://github.com/junioryono/billet
{% if billet_firecracker_enabled %}
# The guest bridges billet-network.service installs only exist for the
# firecracker backend. An ec2 (or docker) node has no such service, and requiring
# one that was never installed would leave the node unit unable to start.
After=network-online.target billet-network.service
Requires=billet-network.service
{% else %}
After=network-online.target
{% endif %}
Wants=network-online.target

{% set billet_notify_ready = billet_systemd_notify_ready | default(false) %}
{% if billet_server_prepare_only | default(false) %}

# HELD, FOR THE SERVER'S REASON RATHER THAN ITS OWN. On a host running both
# roles a CERTLESS node mints the deployment identity when the server has not:
# `billet node` claims the deployment before it reaches --upgrade-probe, and
# nodeDeploymentID falls through to state.DeploymentID(server.state_dir) —
# whose own comment says "whichever role runs first mints the identity". So a
# prepare-only host that held only the server would have the invariant broken
# by the other unit on the same machine.
#
# See billet-server.service for why this is an assertion in the unit rather
# than a mask or a drop-in, and why it asserts that `/` does not exist.
AssertPathExists=!/
{% endif %}

[Service]
Type={{ 'notify' if billet_notify_ready else 'exec' }}
{% if billet_notify_ready %}
NotifyAccess=main
{% endif %}
User=root
Group=root
{% for environment_file in billet_node_environment_files | default([{'path': billet_server_environment_path, 'ignore_errors': true}] if billet_server_environment | default({}) | length > 0 else []) %}
# THE CONTROL PLANE'S ENVIRONMENT, ON A HOST THAT IS BOTH. The updater a rollout
# dispatches to this node inherits this unit's environment, and on a PostgreSQL
# controller it has to open the ledger the server's way; see billet-server.service.
EnvironmentFile={{ '-' if environment_file.ignore_errors else '' }}{{ environment_file.path }}
{% endfor %}
ExecStart=/usr/bin/billet node --config /etc/billet/billet.yaml{{ (' --upgrade-probe' ~ (' --upgrade-probe-hold' if billet_systemd_upgrade_probe_hold | default(false) else '')) if billet_systemd_upgrade_probe | default(false) else '' }}
TimeoutStartSec=120
# billet/registration holds the node's registration record (root-owned, written
# after every accepted registration); a RuntimeDirectory is the one place under
# /run that ProtectSystem=strict leaves writable, and it is the NODE'S ALONE: a
# unit that declares a directory re-owns it recursively at a start where its
# owner differs and removes it at its stop, so a server declaring the same name
# would take the record with it (measured on systemd 255, 2026-09-09).
RuntimeDirectory=billet/locks billet/registration
RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750
TimeoutStopSec=88200
KillSignal=SIGTERM
KillMode=mixed
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5s
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
# The node maps RBD devices and the jailer creates per-guest cgroups through
# sysfs. ProtectKernelTunables would remount those required interfaces read-only.
ProtectKernelModules=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
LockPersonality=true
SystemCallArchitectures=native
ReadOnlyPaths=/etc/billet
# The node atomically replaces its own TLS bundle during renewal. ProtectSystem
# keeps the rest of /etc read-only; only this rotating credential directory is
# writable.
ReadWritePaths=-/etc/billet/tls -/srv/jailer "{{ billet_effective_config.get('node', {}).get('state_dir', '/var/lib/billet/node') }}"

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

billet-server.service.j2.writes: Unreachable on retained route: only dormant candidate/steady-state transaction templates reference it, and binary transactions refuse before ordinary work. No retired controller template is rendered by the retained unit inventory.
billet-server.service.j2.text:
[Unit]
Description=billet control plane
Documentation=https://github.com/junioryono/billet
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
{% if billet_ledger_volume_id | default('') | length > 0 %}
# The ledger lives on a dedicated volume. Without these dependencies, a failed
# mount would let StateDirectory= (and billet itself) create a fresh ledger,
# deployment identity and CA on the root disk — a silent fork of the
# deployment. In the role-managed unit rather than a drop-in, because the
# upgrade transaction refuses drop-ins it cannot replace and recover.
#
# BOTH directives, because they fail differently: Requires= on the EXACT mount
# unit fails the start even when that unit is absent (RequiresMountsFor alone
# is satisfied by the root filesystem when no mount unit exists for the path),
# and RequiresMountsFor= orders the start after every mount the path needs.
# billet_ledger_mount_unit_name is set by the role before any unit render; a
# missing value fails the render rather than emitting a unit with no fence.
Requires={{ billet_ledger_mount_unit_name }}
After={{ billet_ledger_mount_unit_name }}
RequiresMountsFor={{ billet_candidate_server_state_dir }}
{% endif %}
{% if billet_server_prepare_only | default(false) %}

# HELD: this host is prepared to be the control plane but is NOT commissioned.
# The ledger volume is mounted and proved and carries no DEPLOYMENT IDENTITY or
# CA, so starting the server here would mint them — which is indistinguishable
# from a genuinely new deployment and cannot be detected afterwards. (The
# directory is not empty: the role's own `billet check` preflight opens the
# ledger and leaves billet.db and its schema. It does not mint an identity, and
# the identity is the thing that must be absent.)
#
# ASSERT rather than CONDITION deliberately: a failed condition SKIPS the unit
# and reports the start job as successful, which is the wrong signal for a
# deliberate hold. A failed assertion fails the job and logs why.
#
# Disabling the unit is what stops the boot path; this is what stops a manual
# `systemctl start` and anything that pulls the server in as a dependency.
# IN THE UNIT rather than a drop-in for the same reason the mount fence above
# is: the upgrade transaction refuses drop-ins it cannot replace and recover,
# and only this file is staged, backed up, committed and rolled back with the
# transaction.
#
# Release it by converging with billet_server_prepare_only: false.
# ASSERT THAT `/` DOES NOT EXIST. `!` negates, and the root directory exists on
# every running system, so this is false by an immutable property rather than by
# a path nobody happens to have created. The first version asserted a
# /nonexistent/... path, which is conventional, not uncreatable: anything that
# created it would silently commission the host.
AssertPathExists=!/
{% endif %}

{% set billet_notify_ready = billet_systemd_notify_ready | default(false) %}
[Service]
Type={{ 'notify' if billet_notify_ready else 'exec' }}
{% if billet_notify_ready %}
NotifyAccess=main
{% endif %}
User={{ billet_service_user }}
Group={{ billet_service_group }}
UMask=0077
{% if billet_server_environment | default({}) | length > 0 %}
# THE CONTROL PLANE'S ENVIRONMENT, and what it is for is the PostgreSQL ledger:
# `server.state.postgres.dsn_env` names an environment VARIABLE rather than
# carrying a connection string, because a DSN holds a password and a secret in
# billet.yaml ends up in a backup. The file is 0640 root:{{ billet_service_group }},
# which this unit can read and nothing else on the host can.
#
# THE DIRECTIVE IS IN THE UNIT RATHER THAN A DROP-IN, for the same reason the
# mount fence above is: the transactional host upgrade REFUSES effective drop-ins
# it cannot replace and recover, so a DSN delivered that way would break every
# later upgrade of this host.
#
# THE FILE ITSELF IS NOT PART OF THAT TRANSACTION, deliberately. It is operator
# content — a credential, not something a new billet binary changes — so it
# follows the App private key rather than billet.yaml and this unit: nothing
# about a binary upgrade replaces it, so there is nothing for a rollback to put
# back.
#
# WITH THE LEADING `-`, so a host whose file has not been written yet starts
# rather than failing with nothing saying why. billet's own refusal — an empty
# data source — is the better diagnostic, and it names the variable.
EnvironmentFile=-{{ billet_server_environment_path }}
{% endif %}
ExecStart=/usr/bin/billet server --config /etc/billet/billet.yaml{{ (' --upgrade-probe' ~ (' --upgrade-probe-hold' if billet_systemd_upgrade_probe_hold | default(false) else '')) if billet_systemd_upgrade_probe | default(false) else '' }}
TimeoutStartSec=120
TimeoutStopSec=88200
KillSignal=SIGTERM
KillMode=mixed
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5s
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
RestrictNamespaces=true
LockPersonality=true
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true
SystemCallArchitectures=native
SystemCallFilter=@system-service
CapabilityBoundingSet=
ReadOnlyPaths=/etc/billet
ReadWritePaths="{{ billet_candidate_server_state_dir }}"

WantedBy=multi-user.target

ceph-health.sh.j2.writes: /var/lib/billet/health/ceph.last: mktemp in the same health directory, write only its private name, then mv -fT replaces a planted final symlink, including one naming a directory; a symlink is never read as the previous value. mkdir is a constant health directory. mail uses shell-quoted typed mailboxes; SMTP logs to syslog.
ceph-health.sh.j2.text:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

state_dir=/var/lib/billet/health
state_file=${state_dir}/ceph.last
mkdir -p "${state_dir}"

detail=$(ceph health detail 2>&1) || status=ERROR
status=${status:-$(printf '%s\n' "${detail}" | sed -n '1s/ .*//p')}
# A symlink is never read: its target may be an archived secret.
previous=$(test -f "${state_file}" && ! test -L "${state_file}" && cat "${state_file}" || true)

if [ "${status}" != "HEALTH_OK" ] && [ "${detail}" != "${previous}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "${detail}" | mail -r {{ billet_alert_from | quote }} -s "billet Ceph health on $(hostname): ${status}" {{ billet_alert_email | quote }}
elif [ "${status}" = "HEALTH_OK" ] && [ -n "${previous}" ] && ! printf '%s' "${previous}" | grep -q '^HEALTH_OK'; then
    printf '%s\n' "Ceph recovered on $(hostname): ${detail}" | mail -r {{ billet_alert_from | quote }} -s "billet Ceph recovered on $(hostname)" {{ billet_alert_email | quote }}
fi

# Rename replaces a planted ceph.last symlink instead of opening its target;
# -T keeps a symlink to a directory from receiving the file inside it.
state_tmp=$(mktemp "${state_dir}/.ceph.last.XXXXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "${state_tmp}"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
printf '%s\n' "${detail}" >"${state_tmp}"
mv -fT -- "${state_tmp}" "${state_file}"
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
